'''Michael Grätzel''' (born 11 May 1944, in [[Dorfchemnitz]], [[Saxony]], Germany)<ref>Pete Pokkinen: Huippututkija harkitsi nuorena pianistin uraa. Helsingin Sanomat, 10 June 2010, p. B7. (in Finnish)</ref> is a professor at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] where he directs the Laboratory of Photonics and Interfaces. He pioneered research on energy and [[electron transfer]] reactions in mesoscopic-materials and their optoelectronic applications. He co-invented with [[Brian O'Regan (chemist)|Brian O'Regan]] the [[Grätzel cell]] in 1988.<ref name=snaith>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1021/nl071656u| title = Efficiency Enhancements in Solid-State Hybrid Solar Cells via Reduced Charge Recombination and Increased Light Capture| journal = [[Nano Letters]]| volume = 7| issue = 11| pages = 3372–6| year = 2007| last1 = Snaith | first1 = H. J. | authorlink1 = Henry Snaith| last2 = Moule | first2 = A. J. | last3 = Klein | first3 = C. D. | last4 = Meerholz | first4 = K. | last5 = Friend | first5 = R. H. | authorlink5 = Richard Friend| last6 = Grätzel | first6 = M. | authorlink6 = Michael Grätzel | pmid = 17918905| bibcode = 2007NanoL...7.3372S}}</ref><ref>[http://www.millenniumprize.fi/en/2010-prize/professor-michael-graetzel/ Millennium Technology Prize: PROFESSOR MICHAEL GRÄTZEL: DEVELOPER OF DYE-SENSITIZED SOLAR CELLS]</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chem.yale.edu/~cas/tio2.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101125182805/http://www.chem.yale.edu/~cas/tio2.html|url-status=dead|title=Dye-Sensitized Titanium Dioxide|archive-date=25 November 2010}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1021/ar00072a003| title = Artificial photosynthesis: Water cleavage into hydrogen and oxygen by visible light| journal = Accounts of Chemical Research| volume = 14| issue = 12| pages = 376–384| year = 1981| last1 = Graetzel | first1 = M. }}</ref> Grätzel has been called the "father of artificial photosynthesis".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-10-05 |title=PV pioneer Grätzel recognised for 'fundamental contribution' |url=https://optics.org/news/7/10/6 |access-date=2025-04-01 |website=optics.org}}</ref>

Grätzel is the author of over 1000 publications,<ref name=googlescholar>{{GoogleScholar|id=B0h47WAAAAAJ}}</ref> two books and inventor or co-inventor of over 80 patents,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://worldwide.espacenet.com/searchResults?submitted=true&locale=en_EP&DB=EPODOC&ST=advanced&IN=GR%C3%84TZEL+MICHAEL|title=Espacenet – results view|website=worldwide.espacenet.com}}</ref> he has been the Mary Upton Visiting Professor at [[Cornell University]] and a distinguished visiting professor at the [[National University of Singapore]], and is currently a distinguished scientist at [[King Abdulaziz University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dsc.kau.edu.sa/Pages-Distinguished-Scientists.aspx|title=Distinguished Scientists|first=Distinguished|last=Scientists|website=dsc.kau.edu.sa}}</ref> He was an invited professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], the [[École normale supérieure Paris-Saclay]] and [[Delft University of Technology]].

==Education and career==
In 1968 he graduated from [[Free University of Berlin]], in 1971 he earned the Doctor of Philosophy in natural science at [[Technische Universität Berlin]]. In 1976 he completed [[habilitation]] in physical chemistry at the Free University of Berlin. Since 1977 to the present day he is a professor at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] in Lausanne, where he directs the Laboratory of Photonics and Interfaces. He worked as postdoctoral research fellow, lecturer, visiting professor at the [[Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin|Hahn-Meitner Institute]], Free University of Berlin, University of California at Berkeley, Ecole Normale Supérieure de Cachan, Oil and Gas Research Fund, [[University of Notre Dame]] and other educational and research centers. In 1991, he published his breakthrough work in Nature magazine with regard to the new type of solar cells based on a three-dimensional array of tiny (mesoscopic) oxide semiconductor particles with wide band gap covered with an organic pigment that have brought the name of professor into repute and were named as Grätzel cells.
Grätzel is the holder of 10 honorary doctorates in Universities of Asia and Europe: Denmark, Holland, China, Sweden, Singapore and other countries. He is the laureate of tens of prestigious scientific and engineering prizes, such as Grand Prix “Millennium Technology”, Medal of Faraday granted by British Royal Society, Gutenberg Prize, Albert Einstein Prize and others.

Grätzel is a member of the Swiss Chemical Society, the [[Max Planck Society]], and the German Academy of Science (Leopoldina), as well as an honorable member of the Israeli Chemical Society and the Bulgarian Academy of Science, an honorary fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]], and a Fellow of the US-National Academy of Inventors.

==Scientific achievements==
Grätzel is one of the inventors of dye-sensitized solar cells, the so-called Grätzel cells; a new type of solar cell, operating on similar principles as [[photosynthesis]].

==Recognition==
Grätzel's work has been cited over 515,000 times, his [[h-index]] is 315,<ref name=googlescholar/> making him one of the most highly cited chemists in the world.<ref>{{cite web|title=Prof. Michael Graetzel|url=http://lpi.epfl.ch/graetzel|publisher=EPFL|access-date=8 July 2023}}</ref>
He was a frequent guest scientist at the [[National Renewable Energy Laboratory]] (NREL) in [[Golden, Colorado]], was a fellow of the Japanese Society for the Promotion of Science. In 2009 he was named Distinguished Honorary Professor by the Chinese Academy of Science (Changchun) and the Huazhong University of Science and Technology.

Grätzel has received numerous awards including the Millennium 2000 European innovation prize, the 2001 [[Faraday Medal]] of the [[British Royal Society]], the 2001 Dutch Havinga Award, the 2004 Italgas Prize, two McKinsey Venture awards in 1998 and 2002 and the 2005 Gerischer Prize. In 2007 he was awarded the [[Harvey Prize]] of [[Technion]] for pioneered research on energy and electron transfer reactions in mesoscopic-materials and their optoelectronic applications. In 2009 he was awarded the [[Balzan Prize]] for the Science of New Materials. On 9 June 2010, Grätzel received the [[Millennium Technology Prize]], for development of [[dye-sensitized solar cells]]. The cash prize, worth 800,000 [[euro]]s, was awarded, in [[Helsinki]], Finland, by the president of Finland, [[Tarja Halonen]].<ref>{{cite web|title=PROFESSOR GRÄTZEL WINS THE 2010 MILLENNIUM TECHNOLOGY GRAND PRIZE FOR DYE-SENSITIZED SOLAR CELLS |publisher=[[Millennium Technology Prize]] |date=9 June 2010 |url=http://www.millenniumprize.fi/news/165/111/PROFESSOR-GRaeTZEL-WINS-THE-2010-MILLENNIUM-TECHNOLOGY-GRAND-PRIZE-FOR-DYE-SENSITIZED-SOLAR-CELLS/d,news_en/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100613065310/http://www.millenniumprize.fi/news/165/111/PROFESSOR-GRaeTZEL-WINS-THE-2010-MILLENNIUM-TECHNOLOGY-GRAND-PRIZE-FOR-DYE-SENSITIZED-SOLAR-CELLS/d%2Cnews_en/ |archive-date=13 June 2010 |access-date=9 June 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref> His most recent awards include: 2011 Gutenberg Research Award;<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uni-mainz.de/presse/46914.php|title=Strom durch künstliche Photosynthese|website=www.uni-mainz.de}}</ref> 2011 [[Paul Karrer Gold Medal]]; 2011 [[Wilhelm Exner Medal]];<ref>Editor, ÖGV. (2015). Wilhelm Exner Medal. Austrian Trade Association. ÖGV. Austria;</ref> 2012 [[Albert Einstein World Award of Science]];<ref>{{cite web|title=Albert Einstein World Award of Science 2012|url=http://www.consejoculturalmundial.org/winners-science-michaelgratzel.php|access-date=13 August 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131025061728/http://consejoculturalmundial.org/winners-science-michaelgratzel.php|archive-date=25 October 2013}}</ref> and the 2013 [[Marcel Benoist Prize]]. In 2015 he received the [[King Faisal International Prize]] in Chemistry and in 2017 the [[Global Energy Prize]] "for transcendent merits in development of low cost and efficient solar cells, known as “Grätzel cells”, aimed to creation of cost-efficient, large-scale engineering solutions for power generation." In 2020 he received the [[BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Awards|BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Award]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.premiosfronterasdelconocimiento.es/|title=Premios Fronteras del Conocimiento|website=Premios Fronteras}}</ref>

* 2025: [[Pour le Mérite for Sciences and Arts]]<ref name="j280">{{cite web | title=Orden pour le mérite wählt neue Mitglieder hinzu | website=Die Bundesregierung informiert | date=25 July 2025 | url=https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/aktuelles/orden-pour-le-m%C3%A9rite-waehlt-neue-mitglieder-hinzu-2370416 | language=de | access-date=2 October 2025}}</ref>

Grätzel holds honorary doctorates from Faculty of Science and Technology at [[Uppsala University]], [[Sweden]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uu.se/en/about-uu/traditions/prizes/honorary-doctorates/|title=Honorary doctorates – Uppsala University, Sweden|first=David|last=Naylor|website=www.uu.se|date=9 June 2023 }}</ref> (1996), [[University of Turin|Turin]] and [[University of Nova Gorica|Nova Gorica]]. He was elected honorary member of the Société Vaudoise des Sciences Naturelles. Grätzel is a member of the scientific advisory committee at the [[IMDEA]] Nanoscience Institute.
